text:
## Editing products with AI in a spreadsheet

![screenshot showing how to use ai in spreadsheet cells to edit any woocommerce product field](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/21155821/update-with-ai.jpg)

If you want to generate new content or edit existing content in the cells of the spreadsheet, you can do so in two ways:

#### 1- Using a complete prompt

Click on the cell you want to edit, type 
```
ai:
```

 and then enter the prompt. You can use other columns as context or a basis for generating the content. For example:

```
ai: write a short description by summarizing the $Content$
```

#### 2- Using a global prompt shortcut

That is great when you want to trigger AI prompts on the go. But if you want to run the same prompt for multiple cells, the easy way is to use global prompts and trigger them using a prompt shortcut like:

```
ai:write short description
```

text:
## What to consider when using AI for WooCommerce

When using AI to generate or rewrite WooCommerce content, always take some time to review and test the results. Make sure your prompt and chosen LLM are producing content that actually fits your products and helps improve your store. AI can save you a lot of time, but you shouldn’t hand over the entire process without reviewing the output and making changes when necessary.

It’s also important to keep API costs in mind. Depending on the AI provider and model you use, each generation or rewrite may use API credits and add to your bill. These costs are charged by your AI provider, not by WP Sheet Editor, so keep an eye on your usage and choose a model and workflow that work within your budget.

## Why generate WordPress SEO metadata with AI?

Writing an SEO title and meta description for a single post or page is usually manageable. Updating hundreds or thousands of WordPress pages is much more time-consuming. Each piece of metadata needs to accurately describe the page, reflect its search intent, use the target keyword naturally when appropriate, and give searchers a clear reason to consider the result.

Generative AI can speed up the writing stage by creating an initial SEO title or meta description from the existing content, title, and keyword data in your WordPress database. You can then review the generated metadata and adjust anything that does not match your site’s topic, audience, or editorial style.

This is particularly useful when a site has a large backlog of posts with missing SEO titles or meta descriptions. Instead of opening each post individually, you can filter the spreadsheet for missing fields and process the matching rows in bulk.

text:
## AI prompts for generating WordPress SEO titles and meta descriptions

The prompt determines what information the AI uses to create the metadata. The examples below use the existing WordPress title, post content, and target keyword as context. Test the prompts on a small number of posts first, then adjust the instructions to match your site’s audience, writing style, search intent, and SEO requirements.

page_title: How to Bulk Generate SEO Titles and Meta Descriptions with AI in WordPress (Yoast SEO, Rank Math, AIOSEO, SEOPress)
category: Bulk Generate Wordpress Seo Titles Descriptions Ai
heading_path: Prompt for generating SEO titles
text:
### Prompt for generating SEO titles

Use this prompt to create an SEO title from the existing post information. Replace 
```
$Keyword field$
```

 with the exact name of your SEO plugin’s keyword column.

```
Generate a concise, engaging SEO title (50-60 characters) based on the $Title$ and $Content$, ensuring it includes the $Keyword field$. The title should be natural and compelling. Return plain text, free of quotation marks or unnecessary punctuation.
```

page_title: How to Bulk Generate SEO Titles and Meta Descriptions with AI in WordPress (Yoast SEO, Rank Math, AIOSEO, SEOPress)

heading_path: Prompt for generating meta descriptions
text:
### Prompt for generating meta descriptions

Use this prompt to generate a meta description from the SEO title, post content, and target keyword. Replace the placeholders with the exact column names used by your SEO plugin.

```
Generate a compelling SEO description based on the $SEO Title field$ and $Content$, including the $Keyword field$. The description should be engaging, summarize the key points of the post, and encourage reader interest. Keep it under 155 characters for optimal search engine visibility. Return plain text only.
```

**Note about field placeholders:** The placeholder must match the spreadsheet column name exactly, including spaces and punctuation. Wrap the field name in dollar signs. For example, your spreadsheet may use 
```
$AIOSEO Focus Keyphrase$
```

 or 
```
$AIO: Focus Keyphrase$
```

.

If a prompt returns an empty result, check the corresponding spreadsheet column and copy its exact header into the prompt between the dollar signs. This is especially important when different SEO plugins use similar but not identical field names.

### Save your SEO prompts as global prompts

If you plan to generate SEO metadata regularly, save the prompts as global prompts instead of entering the entire instruction every time.

Go to **WP Sheet Editor > AI > Settings > Prompts**, then click **Add new**.

![Adding a new global AI prompt in the WP Sheet Editor AI settings screen](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/31102952/yoast-seo-ai-wp-16.png)

Configure the prompt with these values:

- **Name:** Use a recognizable name such as “SEO Title” or “SEO Description.” After you save it, WP Sheet Editor creates a prompt slug that can be used as a shortcut, such as 
```
ai:seo-title
```

 or 
```
ai:seo-description
```

.
- **Prompt:** Enter the AI instructions and reference the appropriate SEO fields using their exact spreadsheet column names.
- **Save:** Save the prompt so it becomes available from your WordPress spreadsheets.

![Saving the SEO description prompt as a global prompt with its ai:seo-description slug](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/31102905/yoast-seo-ai-wp-18.png)

## Generate SEO titles and meta descriptions directly in the spreadsheet

If you are working with a smaller group of posts, you can generate SEO metadata directly in spreadsheet cells using an **ai:prompt-slug** shortcut. This approach is useful when you want to control which individual rows receive an AI-generated value.

heading_path: Generate SEO titles
text:
### Generate SEO titles

Enter your saved title prompt shortcut in the cells of your plugin’s SEO title column. Depending on the SEO plugin, this may be **SEO Title**, **Rank Math Title**, **AIO: Title**, or **Seopress Titles Title**.

For example, if your saved prompt has the slug **seo-title**, enter:

```
ai:seo-title
```

![The ai:seo-title shortcut entered in a WordPress SEO Title spreadsheet cell](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/31104842/yoast-seo-ai-wp.png)

You can also enter a complete AI prompt directly into a cell:

```
ai:Generate a concise, engaging SEO title (50-60 characters) based on the $Title$ and $Content$, ensuring it includes the $SEO Keyword$. The title should be natural and compelling. Return plain text, free of quotation marks or unnecessary punctuation.
```

A saved shortcut is generally more convenient when you are processing multiple posts because you do not have to paste the full prompt into every cell.

After you enter the shortcut, WP Sheet Editor sends the prompt to the configured AI provider. A loading indicator appears while the AI request is processed.

text:
## Bulk generate WordPress SEO metadata with AI

For a large content library, the **Bulk Edit** workflow is more efficient than entering an AI shortcut row by row. You can first filter your WordPress posts by an SEO field, such as an empty SEO title or meta description, and then apply an AI prompt to every row returned by the search.

This makes it possible to identify missing SEO metadata and generate it in batches rather than opening individual WordPress posts.

WP Sheet Editor also provides a [Bulk AI API](https://wpsheeteditor.com/privacy-policy-bulk-ai-api/) for processing large numbers of AI requests.

heading_path: Do I need to rewrite my AI prompts for each SEO plugin?
text:
### Do I need to rewrite my AI prompts for each SEO plugin?

No. The instructions can remain the same. You mainly need to change the field placeholders so they match the exact column names used by the SEO plugin on your site. For example, you might reference 
```
$SEO Keyword$
```

 for Yoast, 
```
$Rank Math Focus Keyword$
```

 for Rank Math, 
```
$AIO: Focus Keyphrase$
```

 for AIOSEO, or 
```
$Seopress Analysis Target Kw$
```

 for SEOPress. If your spreadsheet uses different column names, use those exact names instead.

## 2. Edit prices in Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel

Open the exported file in Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel and make your pricing changes. You can edit prices manually, use formulas to update multiple products at once, change sale dates, or compare your prices with information from another spreadsheet.

For example, if you want to increase prices by 15%, you can use a formula such as 
```
=C2*1.15
```

 and apply it to the products you want to update. You can also use formulas to add a fixed amount or calculate new prices based on values in other columns.

Using a spreadsheet also makes it easier to share pricing files with vendors, accountants, or assistants without giving them access to your WordPress dashboard.

text:
Increasing prices for WooCommerce products isn’t as easy as it seems. The native WooCommerce editor lets you do this, but there are some issues that large catalogs face. For example, you can only edit selected products, which is limited by the pagination size. Another issue is that WooCommerce isn’t a specialized bulk editor, so you can easily run into timeouts and server errors if you try to raise the prices of hundreds or thousands of products or variations.

That’s why, in this tutorial, we’ll show you how to increase prices by a fixed amount for hundreds or thousands of products. You can edit 1,000 products at a time without any problems, because [WP Sheet Editor](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/woocommerce-spreadsheet/) saves bulk changes in batches, which allows your browser to rest between batches and apply the changes correctly without timeouts.

## Step 2 – Bulk increase prices by fixed amount

In the **Bulk Edit** tool, you need to select these values to increase prices in bulk:

- **Select the rows that you want to update:** It depends on how you have done the product selection. You can edit all the products currently loaded in the spreadsheet (current search) or edit the products that you have manually selected in the spreadsheet.
- **What field do you want to edit:** Select **Regular price**.
- **Select type of edit:** Increase by number.
- **Increase by:** Enter the fixed amount you want to add to your current prices. For example, to add 5 dollars to the current prices, enter 5.
- **Select what you will edit:** In this option you need to decide if you want to **Edit only parent products** or **Edit only variations.**
- Click **Execute Now**.

heading_path: When you may need to increase prices by fixed number
text:
## When you may need to increase prices by fixed number

- **Supplier price increase:** A supplier raises the cost of several products by $3. Instead of updating each product manually, you can add $3 to all of the affected WooCommerce prices at once.
- **Shipping cost increase:** If shipping costs go up, you may need to raise some product prices by $5 to cover the difference. With a spreadsheet, you can make that adjustment across hundreds of products in one go.
- **New handling fee:** If you introduce a $2 handling fee for certain products, you can add that amount to all matching products at once rather than editing them individually.
- **Premium category markup:** You decide to raise the prices of products in a premium category by $10. Filter the products by category and update them all at once.
- **Low-priced products:** You notice that some products under $20 have margins that are too low. You can add $3 to those products without affecting the rest of your catalog.
- **High-value products:** Products over $200 may require extra packaging or insurance. Adding a fixed $25 to their prices can help cover those additional costs.
- **Seasonal adjustment:** Fulfillment costs may incre

- **Seasonal adjustment:** Fulfillment costs may increase during the holiday season. You can temporarily add $5 to selected products and update their prices in bulk.

- **Market adjustment:** Products sold in a specific market may have additional costs that you need to account for. You can filter those products and add a fixed number without changing prices elsewhere.
- **Minimum-margin correction:** After reviewing your catalog, you find that some products have margins that are too low. You can identify those products and add a fixed $4 to each price in bulk.
